checkpoints.summary: Wave 32 release-lane diagnosis of PR #14, read-only. This produces the first hosted production-build evidence for the release branch that does NOT depend on a local credentialed run. The Vercel Git-triggered preview build of d2176904 in project `tourify-beta-k2` passed the production environment contract, passed the Node 24.19.0 / npm 11.17.0 / lockfile v3 toolchain contract, completed `npm ci` (1692 packages, 49s) and completed webpack compilation ('Compiled successfully in 4.4min'). It was then killed by Vercel's maximum build duration: GET /v13/deployments/dpl_2zPXya6iLnXhdgDPeHu7mX3cbQdY reports readyState ERROR, errorCode BUILD_EXCEEDED_MAXIMUM_TIME, plan pro, with buildingAt->ready of 2738.605s = 45.64 minutes, and the last emitted log line is 'Linting and checking validity of types ...'. This is materially new evidence: it demonstrates that the hosted production build environment IS correctly provisioned with all six required production variables and a matching toolchain, so the previously recorded local build:vercel blocker is a LOCAL credential-availability problem, not a build-contract problem. It also establishes a hard new constraint: the Vercel-hosted build path has a 45-minute wall-clock ceiling, and this repository's type/lint phase does not fit inside it while the generated database type surface is drifted. Three determinism defects were recorded and deliberately NOT changed: the repo tracks BOTH package-lock.json (npm, lockfile v3, the enforced contract) and a stale 332KB pnpm-lock.yaml, which the hosted build detected and reported as 'Detected pnpm-lock.yaml 9 ... Using pnpm@10.x based on project creation date'; the hosted project setting is nodeVersion 22.x while engines.node is 24.x and .nvmrc is 24 (engines won at build time, emitting a deprecation warning); and three different declared heap ceilings cover one workload - vercel.json build.env 4096, package.json build:vercel 6144, package.json typecheck 8192 - on a 4-core/8GB Vercel build machine. No memory value was changed: the API reports a timeout and not an OOM, and raising an unproven heap cap on an 8GB box can convert a clean timeout into a hard OOM kill. The CI `Lint And Build` typecheck invocation was also audited and is correct - `NODE_OPTIONS='--max-old-space-size=8192' tsc --noEmit` on a 4-core/16GB ubuntu-latest runner, with zero OOM keywords in the job log.
